title: Arrests and Trials
pdf_title: 12.1.3 17.1 per cent of total arrests were for `Hurt' cases which shared 13.4 per cent of total IPC crime cases in the country. The arrest rate at All-India level declined by 3.7 percent in 1999 over 1998. The arrest rate was highest for Hurt cases (45.2) followed by for Riots (40.2). 12.1.4 Table-63 gives crime head-wise and sex-wise break-up of persons arrested for IPC crimes during the year 1999. The female criminality in the total IPC crimes amounted to 5.6 per cent only. The percentage share of female arrestees was the highest in Dowry Deaths (23.5) followed by Cruelty by Husband or Relatives (22.7) and Hurt (6.0). 12.1.5 State, UT and City-wise details on number of persons arrested during 1998 and 1999 alongwith percentage variations in 1999 over 1998 and also the percentage share of each State and UT to All-India total for arrests during 1999 is given in Table-64. The States, which contributed the highest number of IPC crimes in the country, also contributed highest arrest with similar shares i.e. Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh each sharing 12.0 and 11.5 per cent respectively. In terms of percentage, the increase in the arrested persons during 1999 was the significant in Lakshadweep (283.3%) followed by Sikkim (184.3%). 12.1.6 Table-65 provides the sex-wise details of number of persons arrested under different crimes (IPC) in States, UTs and Cities. The percentage of females arrested under IPC Crimes at All-India level was at 5.6. Goa (12.9%) and Himachal Pradesh (11.6%) recorded comparatively higher share of females in total arrests of the State. Among all States and UTs, Lakshadweep is only UT where no female was involved for committing any IPC crimes. notes: Disposal of persons arrested under the IPC crimes by Police

12.3.1 The crime head-wise details on the disposal of arrested persons are presented in Table-71. During the year, a total of 32,05,267 persons were either under custody or on bail for 23,05,147 various IPC offences under investigation by Police. These also include persons in whose cases the investigations remained pending at the end of year 1998. Out of the total persons, who were under arrest, Police could lay chargesheets in 77.3 per cent; 4.5 per cent persons arrested were either released or freed by Police before trial; 18.3 per cent persons remained under custody or on bail at the end of the year as Police investigation could not be completed in their cases. The highest pendency percentage in the disposal of arrested persons was recorded in cases of `Counterfeiting' (50.6%) followed by `Dacoity' (40.4%) and the lowest was observed in `Sexual Harassment' (8%). In Chargesheeting of arrested persons, police could establish the charge with as high as 90.8 per cent in `Sexual Harassment', followed by `Molestation' (87.1%). The lowest level of charge-sheeting in disposing arrested persons was witnessed in cases of `Counterfeiting' (40.9%) as compared to national average of 77.3% for all IPC crimes.

12.3.2 Table-72 presents State & UT-wise disposal of arrested persons under IPC crimes by Police. Bihar State was responsible for 26.4 per cent pendency in the country followed by West Bengal (11.7%), Andhra Pradesh (10.9%) and Assam (8.4%). The above 4 States accounted for 57.4 per cent of persons under investigation at the end of the year to total persons under investigation at the end of year in the country.
